##### EXERCISE: Restoration—Answers

Answer 1: No—even though they signed their application within the 90-day restoration period, they did not send it until two weeks after the 90-day period had lapsed. The received date is the date the application is physically received at CPC in Canada; however, when it is sent so close to the expiry of the previous document or restoration period, the CPC will go back seven days from the date of receipt as a facilitative measure.

Answer 2: Yes, provided they applied before the end of 90 days from the 18th of November. However, they cannot continue working during this period from the time the work permit expired until if/when they receive approval and a new work permit.

Answer 3: Yes. The CPC in Canada would advise him that he lost his temporary resident status as per A47(b)—working for a different employer which is a condition noted inR185(b)(i), but that he is eligible for restoration. They would have 90 days from the time of notification to submit for restoration.

Answer 4: * Yes. The CPC in Canada would advise him that he lost his temporary resident status as per A47(b)—working at a different location than what was previously authorized.R185(b)(iii) applies in this situation, making them eligible for restoration. They would have 90 days from the time of notification to submit for restoration.

Answer 5: * No—even though the TR sent their application within the 90-day restoration period, they did not comply with the condition: to not work, unless authorized. There has been a failure to comply with a condition other than one imposed under R185(a), R185(b)(i)—(iii)or R185(c), namely a condition imposed underR183(b). The conditions set out atR183are imposed on all temporary residents, whether they know it or not, and a failure to abide by a condition that appears there constitutes a failure to comply with any other conditions imposed.

REVIEW YOUR CURRENT KNOWLEDGE: Conditions on Temporary Residents—Answers Answer 1:

R183 are the general conditions for all temporary residents, no matter if they are issued a document or not.

#### Answer 2:

#### General Conditions—R183

The following conditions are imposed on all temporary residents

### "to leave Canada by the end of the period authorized for their stay"

This is one condition that is always imposed whether it is written out on a TR document or not. You should specify to each temporary resident the length of time they are permitted to remain in Canada. If you fail to

### specify this restriction either verbally or in writing, a time limit is still imposed.

# R183(1)a)

From this it can be seen that if someone is admitted for more than six months, a temporary resident document must be issued. If an examining officer has any apprehension that the foreign national may not leave Canada within the time they specify, then they should document the person's file even if the period is less than six months.

“to not work, unless authorized by this Part or Part 11”

Imposing this condition may serve to discourage a visitor from working illegally; in cases where the officer is apprehensive about the person's true intentions. Also, this condition would serve to strengthen the R183(1)b) department's case against a person who is discovered working in Canada—there will be no arguments about whether or not the prohibition against working had been expressed at the time of documentation.

TR DECISION MAKING / VIRTUAL CLASSROOM PREFACE INSTRUCTOR / PRODUCER GUIDE

# Preface

Course Goal By the end of the course, learners will be able to make decisions on TR applications (visitors, international students, and temporary workers) consistent with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) and the relevant Program Delivery Instructions (PDI)

Prerequisites In this course, the learners build on what they have learned earlier in Introduction to Decision Making (CC8307), e-Introduction to Immigration (CC8200), and Inadmissibility in IRPA (CC7700). To successfully participate in the virtual learning sessions, we recommend that learners take the IRCC Learning Academy course “Getting Ready to Learn in the Virtual Classroom”.

Approach This course combines self-directed learning (eWorkbook and exercise booklet), and group learning (virtual classroom sessions). Learners will complete the content of the eWorkbook and exercise booklet independently, and join the group learning as per the schedule. Scenario reading is required in preparation of each group learning session. These scenarios are included in the participant's guide. The eWorkbook provides the course's informational content. During the group learning sessions, learners practice the concepts learned independently. That is why understanding the importance of self-directed learning is essential for successful participation in the group learning and for course learning outcomes.

### # Review Questions

We learned that paragraph R7(2) lists

4) those that are exempt from the requirement to obtain a TRV. What do these foreign nationals, unless exempted, need to have if they are seeking to enter Canada by Air? Please raise your hand if you know the answer. 5 Foreign nationals in Canada may apply for an extension of their authorization to remain in Canada as a temporary resident if they apply by the end of the period authorized for their stay and if they have complied with all the conditions imposed on their entry into Canada.
### TRUE or FALSE

For those who say TRUE, select a green check mark.

For those who say FALSE, select a red X.

# Answers

If a foreign national is exempt from obtaining a TRV, they are required to obtain an eTA R7.1(1).

R7.1(2) or 7.1(3) identifies those that are exempt from obtaining an eTA.

It is also important to remember that an eTA is required for those travelling to Canada by air and not by land, sea, or by rail.

### TRUE as per paragraph R181(1)

## Additional Resources

The eTA requirement was implemented in 2016 and is linked to the passport that they disclose when they fill in their form. It is valid for five years. It is an automated process and if there are no concerns, the response is given within a few minutes.

A foreign national needs to apply for an eTA online and pay the fees.

Scenario 2 Deulane from Haiti was issued a Super Visa 3 years ago. They have been in Canada for the last 2.5 years and are requesting their first extension to their stay. Private medical insurance is still valid. The applicant has not left Canada since they entered.

# Key Applicant's status-restoration Factors

Length of time in Canada considered Validity of medical insurance

Decision Refuse Foreign national did not apply before their status expired and are not within the restoration period of 90 days. NOTE: The super visa offers parents and grandparents of Canadian Citizen or Permanent Resident children the possibility of visiting Canada for up to 2 years on each entry to Canada. Super visa holders can apply for an extension beyond their initial period granted for their stay but must apply before their status expires and have valid private medical insurance.

### Questions Answers

Scenario 3 Luzhelena is requesting a visitor record extension. Original intention was to visit friends. Has been in Canada for five months and now wants to stay for an additional year as fell in love with a Canadian. No additional information supporting their reasons and finances for an additional year in Canada.

KeyPurpose to spend time with a Canadian friend-no further details on relationship and intentions

## Factors

Funds for stay considered No details regarding activities and/or ties in home country

Decision Refuse-R179(b). Other than having a relationship with a Canadian, no supporting documents relating to funds / employment and intentions for a one-year extension. Refer-for further review of dual intent. NoTE: When assessing dual intent, an officer should distinguish between temporary residence applicants whose intention to fulfill their obligations as a temporary resident (to leave at the end of their period of authorized stay as required by section (R179) is bona fide and an applicant who has no intention of leaving Canada at the end of their authorized stay. In assessing the applicant's intentions, the individual circumstances of the temporary residence applicant must be examined; refusals of non-bona fide temporary residents may only withstand legal challenge when the refusal is based on the information related to the specific application before an officer.

#### Questions Answers

Scenario 4 Ganish received a refusal letter following his request to extend his visitor status in Canada for an additional six months. He arrived in Canada in December and was given a six-month visitor record expiring in June. He applied to extend his status in July but was refused for the sole reason of having lost his status as per A47(a). Following his refusal letter, Ganish sent in an application to restore his status as a visitor and supporting documents demonstrating his ability to support himself as he would like to remain in Canada to continue his journey towards the East Coast. He explained that he was in the Canadian Rockies at the time his status expired and was unable to access the Internet to send his online application.

## KeyLost status as per A47(a)

# Factors

Applied within 90 days following the refusal of his application considered Does he meet the requirements of R182(1)

### Decision Approve

Ganish lost his status as per A47(a) because he did not apply to extend his status prior to the end of the period for which they are authorized to remain in Canada. Although he was refused, he applied to restore his status within the 90 days after he lost his temporary resident status. NOTE: If an application for an extension of temporary resident status under section R181 is refused, the foreign national has 90 days from the date of losing temporary resident status, if otherwise eligible. If an application for an extension is received after the temporary resident status is lost, the case processing centre should refuse the application and respond with a warning notice to the applicant that they are eligible to apply for restoration.

Activity: Credibility Credibility comprises the objective and subjective components of the believability of a foreign national and the documents submitted in support of an application. In the Introduction to Decision Making course as well as in the Inadmissibility Curriculum, officers learned that a part of the assessment of a file, could include a further review of the evidence (i.e. documents, statements) in relation to its reliability and trustworthiness.

### The class will be divided into groups.

The scenarios contain a background of the case and initial assessment of the documents. This is an opportunity to discuss the evidence as a group and identify possible concerns with the case. Allotted time: 20 minutes

Scenario 1: Radbod has submitted a second application to extend their visitor status. Initial reasons and first extension related to visiting relatives. Radbod has been in Canada for one year and is now requesting for an extension to visit his girlfriend. A review of the edoc file has raised concerns.

## Evidence Observations

Address history Girlfriend's address since entry to Canada

## Financial statementsContinual cash deposits every 2-3 weeks estimating $500-$700 for the past 3 months

GCMS information on girlfriendThe girlfriend submitted a previous spousal sponsorship application two years ago that was refused. The application was for the sponsorship of a different person than the foreign national in question.

# Address historyGirlfriend's address since entry to Canada

Concerns

Current activities-intended to visit family but has been staying with a girlfriend who was not mentioned upon entry and previous extension request Finances-concerned regarding the source of cash deposits (possibly working in Canada) Relationship with girlfriend -intentions with relationship as no details regarding relationship itself was mentioned previously Integrated search on girlfriend shows she tried to sponsor a spouse before-is she still married, reasons for divorce, etc.

Scenario 2: Rochelle has submitted an application for a visitor record extension to visit Canadian citizen son in Cavendish, Prince Edward Island. Rochelle has been in Canada for the past two years. She has received one extension and has maintained her status. Rochelle wants to continue her stay in Canada to help with her son and future daughter-in-law's wedding planning and to be there for this milestone. The wedding will take place in a few months. You review bank statements showing regular monthly pension deposits but for the past eight months there are biweekly deposits between $200 and $300. You see an Info Alert that describes work without authorization allegations. The Info Alert is a letter describing that Rochelle is working as a personal support worker for an elderly neighbour. The letter further outlines Rochelle's job duties and that the neighbour pays her a mix of cash and e-transfers. A review of the edoc file has raised concerns.

# Concerns

Possibly working without authorization and misrepresentation-affects the credibility of the foreign national for not disclosing employment and/or having sufficient funds for stay in Canada (bank deposits-monthly pension with recent biweekly deposits).

# 10.0 Debriefing on Credibility (15 minutes)

Instructor:

Refer to Activity: Credibility to review the scenario with the learners and comment accordingly.

“Let's listen to your presentations and discuss the scenarios together. Whose group is going to present first?" Please raise your hands.

Discuss the learners' comments, and provide examples when needed. Reiterate to participants that credibility has to do with the veracity, usually of the person, but could be applied to a document. Reliability is maybe closer to accuracy, neutrality etc. You could therefore have a credible applicant that provides information that is not reliable. The term credibility is best used where one would not believe something because it is possibly a lie, fraud or misrepresentation. Whenever the applicant's credibility or the credibility of their documents is in question, it is imperative that procedural fairness is engaged by providing the applicant the opportunity to respond by sending a Procedural Fairness Letter or through an interview. It is not generally necessary to proceed with procedural fairness for information that is unreliable, but it is necessary to proceed with procedural fairness if there are credibility concerns.

Ask whether the learners have any questions. Answer their questions and elaborate on details when needed. Advise learners, references will be included in the answer key.

“In your workbooks, you learned that there are two components that are reviewed in every application: (1) eligibility and (2) admissibility. We just finished examining the eligibility requirements and also reviewed the topic of credibility. If there are no questions at this point, we will now move onto the next component and learn about inadmissibility".

Background information: Poonam and her spouse entered Canada on TRVs in which Poonam was approved as a cergy leader [R1s()] for a gurdwara in Clareshoim Alberta. There were given one-year visitor status. In their TRV application, a letter from the gurdwara in Canada outlined the duties for providing spiritual counseling and functions reiating to the gathering of the congregation while the letter from home gurdwara confirmed position in their ministry. Instructor:

Refer to Activity: Performance Activity. "I hope you had a moment to refresh, stretch your legs or grab a snack. Now, we

## are going to do the performance activity, the last activity for today's session. We

## are going to apply everything that we have learned so far."

Give clear instructions how to work on the performance activity.

1. Explain to the learners that you are going to show and read a multi-part scenario out to them. Each part will introduce incremental changes in the circumstances of the applicants. At each development, they need to “take a stand" on their decision on the case by using the pointer tool from the annotation toolbar and by clicking in the approve, refuse or refer column.
2. It is not incorrect to say that answers may vary, for example where officers must be satisfied on balance of probabilities (ex.: R179(b)). However, an answer that goes against the Act and Regulations (ex.: declaring someone inadmissible when they are not and vice versa) or that is contrary to natural justice / procedural fairness (ex.: discrimination) can not be a right answer. Ask if instructions are clear for learners.
3.Begin reading the first part of the scenario and ask learners make a decision by selecting the pointer tool and clicking in the approve, refuse or refer column.

4. Observe the decisions on the screen. Encourage learners not to “sit on the fence" so to speak – they are to take a position. This is for the purpose of the exercise but that in real life the procedural fairness principles and reasonableness standard command that a decision-maker considers all the facts.
5. Invite learners to explain their rational. Refer to the answer key and debriefing points of the performance activity to provide feedback. Keep the discussion respectful, positive and focused on learning the implication of the policy. Help to prevent learners who are in the minority group feeling defensive by rephrasing comments in a positive manner when necessary. Ideally, there should be a good exchange of ideas that help to clarify the policy. “On this slide, you will see the first part of the scenario that we are going to work on. She was sent a request to provide additional copy of a valid passport and proof of funds and was given 7 days to provide these documents. It has been two weeks and no documents have been submitted.

# KeyFunds-ongoing bi-weekly deposits for past year but stopped six months ago

Factors considered No tuition receipt No valid passport Decision1. Refuse. R179(c), A16(1), R217(2)- does not meet eligibility requirements, specifically foreign national does

not have a valid passport.

## Questions Answers

Scenario 2 Mohammed recently graduated from with a diploma in Business Administration. He is now requesting a study permit to attend He provided an LOA with a scholarship valued at $5,000. The applicant provided bank statements, transcripts from proof of program completion, lease agreement and a valid passport. Cross-reference shows that applicant's accompanying spouse has not applied for an extension to their visitor record. Visitor record expired last month. No information provided to indicate spouse left Canada. Bank statement is a joint account with spouse.

# Key LOA for new school

Factors Logical progression of studies considered Funds – scholarship, joint account with spouse

Decision 1. Approve. Despite concerns with accompanying spouse, sufficient evidence provided to satisfy R217 for this application. Continual pursuit of business degree. Although funds are from joint account, partial scholarship and foreign national has the ability to work part-time on-campus and off-campus.

2. Refer the file for further review regarding spouse's intention to remain in Canada. Funds are from joint account with spouse. However, applicant would not be an inadmissible family member as per A42(1). NOTE: A42(1) inadmissibility applies only when a foreign national applying for temporary residence has a family member who is inadmissible under A34, A35 or A37, whether the family member is accompanying the foreign national or not.

Activity: Credibility Credibility comprises the objective and subjective components of the believability of a foreign national and the documents submitted in support of an application. In your introduction to Decision Making course as well as in the Inadmissibility Curriculum, you learned that a part of the assessment of a file could include a further review of the evidence (i.e. documents, statements) in relation to its reliability and trustworthiness. The scenarios contain a background of the case and initial assessment of the documents. This is an opportunity to discuss the evidence as a group and identify possible concerns with the case. The class will be divided into groups. Allotted time: 10 minutes

# How to use the Participant Guide

The Participant Guide contains scenarios that you will work on during the group learning sessions. For better learning experience, we recommend reading the scenarios and making your notes before the group learning session. During the virtual or classroom sessions, you will have opportunities to participate in group discussions and activities, ask questions, and benefit from exchange with your peers and instructors. The Participant Guide also contains handouts for the presentations that will be displayed to you at the sessions. Answers to the scenarios will be sent to you after the sessions by email.

# Section 3.0 – Credibility

Credibility comprises the objective and subjective components of the believability of a foreign national and the documents submitted in support of an application. In the Introduction to Decision Making course as well as in the Inadmissibility Curriculum, officers learned that a part of the assessment of a file, could include a further review of the evidence (i.e. documents, statements) in relation to its reliability and trustworthiness. The class will be divided into groups. The scenarios contain a background of the case and initial assessment of the documents. This is an opportunity to discuss the evidence as a group and identify possible concerns with the case. Allotted time: 20 minutes

### TR Decision Making

### Questions Answers

Scenario 4 Ganish received a refusal letter following his request to extend his visitor status in Canada for an additional six months. He arrived in Canada in December and was given a six-month visitor record expiring in June. He applied to extend his status in July but was refused for the sole reason of having lost his status as per A47(a). Following his refusal letter, Ganish sent in an application to restore his status as a visitor and supporting documents demonstrating his ability to support himself as he would like to remain in Canada to continue his journey towards the East Coast. He explained that he was in the Canadian Rockies at the time his status expired and was unable to access the Internet to send his online application.

# KeyLost status as per A47(a)

## Factors

Applied within 90 days following the refusal of his application considered Does he meet the requirements of R182(1)

## Decision Approve

Ganish lost his status as per A47(a) because he did not apply to extend his status prior to the end of the period for which they are authorized to remain in Canada. Although he was refused, he applied to restore his status within the 90 days after he lost his temporary resident status. NOTE: If an application for an extension of temporary resident status under section R181 is refused, the foreign national has 90 days from the date of losing temporary resident status, if otherwise eligible. If an application for an extension is received after the temporary resident status is lost, the case processing centre should refuse the application and respond with a warning notice to the applicant that they are eligible to apply for restoration.

## TR Decision Making

Scenario 2

Rochelle has submitted an application for a visitor record extension to visit Canadian citizen son in Cavendish, Prince Edward Island. Rochelle has been in Canada for the past two years. She has received one extension and has maintained her status. Rochelle wants to continue her stay in Canada to help with her son and future daughter-in-law's wedding planning and to be there for this milestone. The wedding will take place in a few months.

You review bank statements showing regular monthly pension deposits but for the past eight months there are biweekly deposits between $200 and $300. You see an Info Alert that describes work without authorization allegations. The Info Alert is a letter describing that Andrea is working as a personal support worker for an elderly neighbour. The letter further outlines Rochelle's job duties and that the neighbour pays her a mix of cash and e-transfers.

A review of the edoc file has raised concerns.

Concerns

Possibly working without authorization and misrepresentation-affects the credibility of the foreign national for not disclosing employment and/or having sufficient funds for stay in Canada (bank deposits-monthly pension with recent biweekly deposits).

Scenario 3 Fatma is visiting her spouse who has been in Canada for two years on a four-year study permit. Fatma's visitor status will expire within one month as she only received six months visitor status because she told the POE and overseas office that her intention was to come to Canada to visit her spouse and return home after one month based on her vacation leave from work. She is requesting for an extension to her visitor record to coincide with the two years remaining duration of her spouse's study permit. No indication from her employer that she has received an extension to her leave. Info Alert noted applicant was refused entry to the US last month. The applicant did not disclose US refusal. Insufficient proof of funds provided to support both Fatma and her husband while they remain in Canada. She provided a letter addressing why she wants to remain in Canada as she has limited family back home, has no intention to work in Canada as she has minimal English language skills, husband will provide support as he works part-time at a grocery store (off-campus employment).

File referred for further review.

Poonam and her spouse intended to come to Canada for one year. It was also noted the couple has had work related travels across the country and the couple has no dependents.

Their permits are about to expire so they are asking for one-year extension. Poonam explained both her and

her husband are still needed in their temple. She continues with her spiritual duties while her spouse continues to do community service in the gurdwara. Accommodations and living expenses continue to be provided by the gurdwara. Maintained status

# Key Points ExerciseLearning

Academy Question 4 of 10 Answer:

We learned that paragraph R7(2) lists those that are exempt from the requirement to obtain a TRV. What do these foreign nationals, unless exempted, need to have if they are seeking to enter Canada by Air?

If a foreign national is exempt from obtaining a TRV, they are required to obtain an eTA R7.1(1). R7.1 (2) or 7.1(3) identifies those that are exempt from obtaining an eTA.

It is also important to remember that an eTA is required for those travelling to Canada by air and not by land, sea, or by rail. VISITOR APPLICATIONS – TR DECISION MAKING | Visual Aid 05 (cont)

# Key Points

As per R9(1), all foreign nationals are required to obtain a study permit for engaging in academic, professional, vocational or other education or training that is more than six months in duration at a DLI in Canada, unless exempted

A foreign national is exempt from a study permit requirement if they are described as being authorized to study without the issuance of a study permit in R188 or A30(2)

A foreign national can apply for a study permit before entry, on entry or after entry (R213, R214 and R215) To be eligible for a study permit, a foreign national needs to meet the general requirements for all temporary residents R179 as well as the specific requirements of R216 or R217

A study permit cannot be issued without LOA or conditional LOA R219(1), unless exempted under R219(2) Students may be eligible to work on R186(f) or off campus R186(v) and be part of other work programs. Only full-time students can work on or off campus.
